title: A finite surjection splits finitely many separated etale maps into opens
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $(u_i:U_i\to S)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of separated etale morphisms of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There exists a finite surjective morphism $r:T\to S$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that for every $i\in I$ there are a finite set $J_i$, quasi-compact open subschemes $W_{ij}\subseteq T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and a $T$-isomorphism
$$U_i\times_ST\simeq\coprod_{j\in J_i}W_{ij}.$$
The maps from the summands to $T$ are their open immersions. The opens $W_{ij}$ need not be disjoint as subsets of $T$ and need not cover $T$. Empty $U_i$ and the empty family are allowed. Fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Orgogozo author draft, Lemma 9.1.3 and its proof, printed p. 20; the finite-family version follows by successive finite surjective base changes. Local archival PDF WANTED; source read online.

proof.text: First prove the single-map assertion by induction on a bound $d$ for geometric fibre cardinalities, simultaneously for every Noetherian base $B$ and every separated etale finite-presentation $v:E\to B$; no surjectivity of $v$ is assumed. Such $E$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], hence quasi-compact. On affine charts [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-quasi-finite] gives local quasi-finiteness, so [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-qc-source-bounded-fibres] bounds the degrees of its fibres. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-base-change] the same bound holds after extension to algebraically closed fields. Each geometric fibre is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] identifies its algebra with a finite product of copies of that algebraically closed field, so degree equals geometric cardinality. Thus some $d$ suffices for every input. If $d=0$, $E$ has no points and is empty; the identity of $B$ and the empty coproduct solve this case. For $d>0$ assume the assertion for bound $d-1$ over every Noetherian base and fix $u:U\to S$ with bound $d$.

source.place: Tag 03JA (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded); geometric-degree identification as in more-morphisms.tex Tag 09Z0 (lemma-there-is-a-scheme-integral-over), first induction paragraph; Orgogozo Lemma 9.1.3, printed p. 20.

proof.text: The base $S$ is qcqs: quasi-compact by hypothesis and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Since $u$ is separated, finite type and everywhere quasi-finite by Step 1, [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] gives $U\hookrightarrow Y\to S$ with the first arrow a quasi-compact open immersion and the second finite. Here $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [sk-lem-nagata-sketch-closure] to replace $Y$ by the scheme-theoretic closure $\overline U$ of $U$. Its closed immersion into $Y$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so $p:\overline U\to S$ remains finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and $\overline U$ remains Noetherian. Write $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$. This open is dense: a nonempty open disjoint from $U$ would contradict injectivity of $\mathcal O_{\overline U}\to j_*\mathcal O_U$, since its unit section would map to zero. Finally $p$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres].

source.place: Tag 05K0 (lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite); morphisms.tex Tag 01RG (lemma-quasi-compact-immersion); Orgogozo Lemma 9.1.3, Zariski-main factorization.

proof.text: Put $P=U\times_S\overline U$, with projections $a$ to $U$ and $b$ to $\overline U$, and consider the graph $\gamma=(1,j):U\to P$. It is closed: the square with top arrow $j:U\to\overline U$, bottom arrow $(ja,b):P\to\overline U\times_S\overline U$, and right arrow $\Delta_p$ is Cartesian by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The separatedness definition [def-weil-proper-morphism] makes $\Delta_p$ closed, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes $\gamma$ closed. It is open: inside the open subscheme $U\times_SU\subset P$ it is $\Delta_u$, an open immersion by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-weil-unramified-morphism]; that subscheme is open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Thus, writing $W$ for the complementary open-and-closed subscheme, we have $P=U\amalg W$ over $\overline U$, with first structure map $j$. The map $w:W\to\overline U$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. It is separated because its diagonal is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $b$, which is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change]. The map $b$ is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], so $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The open $W$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Hence $w$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], and, being separated and etale, is of finite presentation. It is quasi-finite by the same affine-chart argument as Step 1.

source.place: Tag 01KS (lemma-semi-diagonal), proved here by pulling back the separated diagonal; morphisms.tex Tags 02GE (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale), 02GN (lemma-composition-etale); more-morphisms.tex Tag 09Z0, diagonal-complement paragraph.

proof.text: For a geometric point of the dense open $U\subset\overline U$, the fibre of $P\to\overline U$ is the corresponding fibre of $u$, with at most $d$ points. The graph summand contributes exactly one point, so the fibre of $w$ has at most $d-1$ points there. To extend this bound, apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-qf-stratification] to $w$, which is flat and locally of finite presentation because it is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and is separated and quasi-finite by Step 3. Let its closed sets be $Z_r$. The universal property applied to residue-field points says that $Z_r$ is exactly the locus of fibre degree at most $r$: every point lies in one stratum and its fibre degree is that stratum's index. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-base-change], etale base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], and the product-of-separable-fields description [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product], this degree is also the geometric fibre cardinality. Consequently $Z_{d-1}$ contains $U$ and, being closed, equals $\overline U$. The induction hypothesis of Step 1 now applies to $w:W\to\overline U$: its base is Noetherian, its morphism has all the required properties, and its bound is $d-1$. Obtain a finite surjection $q:T'\to\overline U$ and an isomorphism $W\times_{\overline U}T'\simeq\coprod_{\ell\in L}A_\ell$ with $L$ finite and each $A_\ell\subseteq T'$ a quasi-compact open. This is an actual application of the smaller-bound assertion, with no surjectivity hypothesis on $w$.

source.place: Tags 07RY (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-lqf-universally-bounded) and 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf); Tag 09Z0, strict fibre-degree calculation, adapted to the splitting induction of Orgogozo Lemma 9.1.3.

proof.text:
The image $u(U)$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. Let $C=(S\setminus u(U))_{\mathrm{red}}$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], and take $T_u=T'\amalg C$. Its map to $S$ is finite: $T'\to S$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], and $C\to S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]; over an affine of $S$, their disjoint union is the spectrum of the product of two finite algebras, again a finite algebra [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. It is surjective: a point in $u(U)$ lifts to $U\subset\overline U$ and then along $q$, and every other point lifts to $C$. Base changing the decomposition of Step 3 along $q$ gives, by [def-pc-fibre-product],
$$U\times_ST'\simeq (U\times_{\overline U}T')\amalg(W\times_{\overline U}T')\simeq V\amalg\coprod_{\ell\in L}A_\ell,$$
where $V=q^{-1}(U)$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Since $T'$ is finite over the Noetherian $\overline U$, it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; thus $V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Moreover $U\times_SC=\varnothing$, since its underlying points would map both into $u(U)$ and its complement. Pullback distributes over this finite disjoint union, so the same displayed coproduct, viewed as opens in the component $T'\subset T_u$, is $U\times_ST_u$. Their maps to $T_u$ are open immersions. This completes the induction and the single-map assertion, including $d=1$ via the $d-1=0$ case.

proof.text:
If $I$ is empty, take $T=S$ and all coproducts empty. Otherwise, for each
$i\in I$ repeat the five preceding single-map steps for $U_i\to S$. We obtain a
finite surjection $r_i:T_i\to S$, a finite index set $J_i$, quasi-compact
opens $W_{ij}\subseteq T_i$, and an isomorphism
$U_i\times_ST_i\simeq\coprod_{j\in J_i}W_{ij}$ over $T_i$. The auxiliary
statement includes the cases $U_i=\varnothing$ and $J_i=\varnothing$.

source.place: Orgogozo author draft, Lemma 9.1.3 and its proof, printed p. 20; apply the single-map construction to each member of the finite family.

proof.text: Take the iterated fibre product $T=\prod_{i\in I}T_i$ over $S$, with the empty product interpreted as $S$. By repeated application of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], the map $T\to S$ and each projection $p_i:T\to T_i$ are finite. Each factor $T_i\to S$ is surjective, so [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and composition of surjective maps show inductively that $T\to S$ is surjective as well.

For each $i$, pull back the isomorphism of Step 6 along $p_i:T\to T_i$. Associativity of fibre products and their compatibility with disjoint open unions identify the pullback as
$$U_i\times_ST\simeq\coprod_{j\in J_i}(W_{ij}\times_{T_i}T).$$
These identities follow directly from the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], or by restricting to each open summand and gluing. Each summand maps to $T$ by an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change].

source.place: Orgogozo Lemma 9.1.3, finite-family base-change consequence; morphisms of open subschemes under pullback.

proof.text: Each $W_{ij}$ is quasi-compact by the single-map construction of Step 5, used in Step 6. Cover it by finitely many affine opens. The inverse image of each under the finite map $p_i:T\to T_i$ is affine: the restricted map is finite by part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], and its source is affine by part (b). Thus $W_{ij}\times_{T_i}T$ is covered by finitely many affines and is quasi-compact. This proves all required clauses for the common finite surjection $T\to S$. The coproduct summands need not be disjoint as subsets of $T$ or cover $T$, and the construction also covers empty members and the empty family.

Step 2 checks the ZMT and Nagata-closure hypotheses; finite gives finite type and Noetherian gives quasi-separated in one line each, and the topological-density argument is correct. In Step 3 the graph is closed (pullback of the diagonal of p, i.e. 01KS proved in the step) and open (the diagonal of u inside the open U x_S U), and W is étale, separated, qc and fp. Step 4: the 07RZ universal property tested on residue fields shows that {degree <= r} is closed, so Z_{d-1} = Ubar; quasi-finiteness holds since the fibres are finite and discrete. The induction then genuinely applies to W -> Ubar without surjectivity. Step 5: T' ⊔ (S - u(U))_red is finite and surjective, U x_S T' = q^{-1}(U) ⊔ W x T' = V ⊔ ⊔A_l, and U x_S C is empty. Steps 6-9: the finite surjective fibre product over S, pullback of the splitting, and qc via affine preimages under the finite maps.
